prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1307; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane on the highway in Pearland, Texas, when Driver 2 moved from the center lane into the same space without signaling. The front passenger side of Driver 2's vehicle struck the rear driver side of Driver 1's vehicle, pushing it toward the shoulder. Both drivers pulled over safely. I spoke with Driver 1, Driver 2, and Passenger, who was seated beside Driver 1 at the time. Driver 2 acknowledged changing lanes without checking the mirror. Two independent witnesses in nearby vehicles described the same sequence, and each stated they saw the impact clearly. Scene photographs show scraping and deformation along the rear driver side panel of Driver 1's vehicle, consistent with the direction and force of the contact. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness shortly after the collision, which is a common response to a sideswipe impact of this kind. Officers observed no prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 is a member of the same household as the policyholder, and the policyholder's records list Driver 1 as a regular driver. Passenger was also present and reported no injuries at the scene.
